items.title: Section: The Fourth Gate Opens — Elements That Never Betray Their Own Nature, and Why a Greedy Mind Cannot Feel Free

items.zh: 云何第四處非處門差別？謂無處無位地捨自相成餘界相，無有是處；不捨自相，斯有是處。如地，如是餘大種，如應當知。無處無位生長欲界不得天眼見諸天色，無有是處；見人中色，斯有是處。如是餘根，如應當知。無處無位有貪愛者，貪愛覆蔽、貪愛未斷，而於財利心離染著，無有是處；如是瞋、癡，隨應當知。
items.en: What distinguishes the fourth gate of the valid and the invalid? There is no place, no circumstance, in which earth could relinquish its own characteristic and take on the characteristic of another element — this is not valid; that it does not relinquish its own characteristic is valid. As with earth, so too, by analogy, should the remaining great elements be understood. There is no place, no circumstance, in which one born and matured in the desire realm, without the heavenly eye, could see the forms of the heavens — this is not valid; that one sees the forms of the human realm is valid. As with this, so too, by analogy, should the remaining faculties be understood. There is no place, no circumstance, in which one whose mind is covered by greed, whose greed remains unsevered, could nonetheless be free of attachment towards wealth and gain — this is not valid; the opposite of this is valid. As with this, so too, by analogy, should hatred and delusion be understood.

items.title: Section: No Genuine Meditation Without First Subduing Affliction, and What It Truly Means to See the Buddha

items.zh: 無處無位不斷貪等一切煩惱、隨煩惱、纏修四念住，無有是處；與此相違，斯有是處。如修念住，如是所餘菩提分法，當知亦爾。無處無位於如來所不捨諍見、諍欲、諍心，若不開許，而能正面覩於如來，無有是處；若捨、若許，斯有是處。
items.en: There is no place, no circumstance, in which one could cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness while not having severed greed and every other root and secondary affliction currently manifest — this is not valid; the opposite of this is valid. As with the foundations of mindfulness, so too should the remaining factors of enlightenment be understood. There is no place, no circumstance, in which one who has not relinquished contentious views, contentious desires, and a contentious mind in the Buddha's presence, and whom the Buddha has not sanctioned, could genuinely behold the Buddha face to face — this is not valid; that one relinquishes these, or is sanctioned by the manner the Buddha permits, is valid.

items.title: Section: Why the Buddha Never Loses Track of a Single Being, and Bodhisattvas Who Never Turn Back

items.zh: 無處無位一切智者、一切見者有所知境而不了知，或復失念作非一切智者所作，無有是處；與此相違，斯有是處。無處無位已入大地諸菩薩等，於諸有情起故害心，或菩提心當有退轉，無有是處；與此相違，斯有是處。如是等類，應當觀察第四處非處門差別之相。
items.en: There is no place, no circumstance, in which an all-knowing, all-seeing one could fail to comprehend a knowable object, or could lose mindfulness and act as a non-omniscient being would — this is not valid; the opposite of this is valid. There is no place, no circumstance, in which bodhisattvas who have entered the ground levels could deliberately give rise to harmful intent towards beings, or could regress from the awakening-mind — this is not valid; the opposite of this is valid. Cases such as these should be observed as illustrating the fourth gate's own distinguishing characteristic.

items.title: Section: Eight Ways to Examine the Valid and Invalid, and What Truly Separates This Topic from Dependent Origination

items.zh: 復次，略有四處四非處，依前所說觀待道理、作用道理、證成道理、法爾道理，應正觀察。若於如是所說道理不相違背示現宣說，是名為處；若此相違示現宣說，是名非處。如是四處，并前所說，合成八種處非處善巧。問：緣起善巧、處非處善巧何差別？答：唯於因果生起道理正智顯了，名緣起善巧。若於一切無顛倒理正智顯了，名處非處善巧。所餘處非處善巧決擇，文不復現。
items.en: Next, in brief there are four further kinds of valid and four of invalid, to be correctly observed according to the principle of relativity, the principle of function, the principle of proof, and the principle of intrinsic nature already spoken of earlier. Whatever is taught and revealed without contradicting these principles is called valid; whatever is taught and revealed in contradiction to them is called invalid. These four, together with what was said before, make eight kinds of skilful understanding of the valid and the invalid. Question: what distinguishes the skilful understanding of dependent origination from the skilful understanding of the valid and the invalid? Answer: clearly revealing, through correct wisdom, only the principle by which cause and effect arise is called the skilful understanding of dependent origination. Clearly revealing, through correct wisdom, the undistorted principle underlying all things is called the skilful understanding of the valid and the invalid. The remaining decisions concerning the skilful understanding of the valid and the invalid do not appear again in this text.

items.title: Section: From One Faculty to a Hundred and Twenty — Why the Buddha Settled on Exactly Twenty-Two

items.zh: 如是已說處非處善巧。根善巧我今當說。總嗢拕南曰：初義意、建立、廣分別、為後。
items.en: Thus the skilful understanding of the valid and the invalid has been explained. The skilful understanding of the faculties shall now be explained. The summary verse states: name and meaning, purpose, and establishment come first; extensive analysis comes after.

items.title: Section: What "Faculty" Actually Means — Eight Angles on a Single Word

items.zh: 問：何等是根義？答：增上義是根義。
items.en: Question: what is the meaning of "faculty"? Answer: dominant meaning is the meaning of "faculty." Question: why is it called a faculty? What is the meaning of "faculty"? Answer: dominant meaning is the meaning of faculty; illuminating meaning is the meaning of faculty; manifesting meaning is the meaning of faculty; the meaning of being joyfully beheld is the meaning of faculty; dignified meaning is the meaning of faculty; foremost meaning is the meaning of faculty; supreme meaning is the meaning of faculty; sovereign meaning is the meaning of faculty.

items.title: Section: Why Twenty-Two, Not Any Other Number — the Six Functions That Establish Every Faculty

items.zh: 問：為顯何義？答：為顯於彼彼事彼彼法最勝義。云何建立二十二根？謂能取境增上義故，建立六根。安立家族相續不斷增上義故，建立二根。為活性命事業方便增上義故，建立一根。受用業果增上義故，建立五根。世間清淨增上義故，建立五根。出世清淨增上義故，建立三根。
items.en: Question: for what purpose are the faculties revealed? Answer: to reveal the supreme significance each has within its own respective domain of things and phenomena. How are the twenty-two faculties established? Because of the dominant significance of grasping an object, six faculties are established. Because of the dominant significance of ensuring an unbroken family lineage, two faculties are established. Because of the dominant significance of the means by which life's activities continue, one faculty is established. Because of the dominant significance of experiencing the fruit of karma, five faculties are established. Because of the dominant significance of mundane purification, five faculties are established. Because of the dominant significance of transcendent purification, three faculties are established.

items.title: Section: A Second Way to Count the Faculties Through Experience, and the Cosmic Origin of Male and Female

items.zh: 復次，受用顯境增上義故，建立六根。受用隱境增上義故，建立二根。受用境界時分邊際增上義故，建立一根。受用境界發生雜染增上義故，建立五根。安立清淨增上義故，建立八根。復次，顯於內門受用境界增上義故，建立六根。顯於外門受用境界增上義故，建立二根。受用內身增上義故，建立一根。
items.en: Next, because of the dominant significance of experiencing manifest objects, six faculties are established. Because of the dominant significance of experiencing hidden objects, two faculties are established. Because of the dominant significance of the temporal boundary within which objects are experienced, one faculty is established. Because of the dominant significance of affliction arising through the experience of objects, five faculties are established. Because of the dominant significance of establishing purification, eight faculties are established. Next, in order to reveal experiencing objects through an inward-facing gate, six faculties are established. In order to reveal experiencing objects through an outward-facing gate, two faculties are established. Because of the dominant significance of experiencing the inward body, one faculty is established.

items.title: Section: A Third Pass — Establishing the Faculties Through What the Body Itself Depends On

items.zh: 受用外境及與內身發生雜染增上義故，建立五根。對治雜染、安立清淨增上義故，建立八根。復次，依止端嚴增上義故，建立五根。能令依止隨自在轉增上義故，建立一根。依止安住增上義故，建立一根。依止出生增上義故，建立二根。依止損益增上義故，建立五根。依止解脫增上義故，建立八根。
items.en: Because of the dominant significance of affliction arising through both outer objects and the inner body, five faculties are established. Because of the dominant significance of counteracting affliction and establishing purification, eight faculties are established. Next, because of the dominant significance of the bodily support appearing dignified, five faculties are established. Because of the dominant significance of enabling that support to move freely at its own command, one faculty is established. Because of the dominant significance of that support abiding for its span, one faculty is established. Because of the dominant significance of that support's capacity to generate life, two faculties are established. Because of the dominant significance of that support being benefited or harmed, five faculties are established. Because of the dominant significance of that support achieving liberation, eight faculties are established.

items.title: Section: A Fourth Pass — What "Surpassing Rebirth" and "Decisive Superiority" Actually Mean

items.zh: 復次，顯有情事增上義故，建立六根。生有情事增上義故，建立二根。令有情事若住、若沒增上義故，建立一根。顯諸有情受用境界增上義故，建立五根。顯諸有情勝生方便增上義故，建立五根。顯諸有情定勝方便增上義故，建立三根。
items.en: Next, because of the dominant significance of revealing a being's own existence, six faculties are established. Because of the dominant significance of generating a being's existence, two faculties are established. Because of the dominant significance of a being's existence abiding or perishing, one faculty is established. Because of the dominant significance of revealing how a being experiences objects, five faculties are established. Because of the dominant significance of the means to a being's surpassing rebirth, five faculties are established. Because of the dominant significance of the means to a being's decisive superiority, three faculties are established.

items.zh: 復次，顯有情事增上義故，建立六根。

blocks.text: The last examples of the impossible, and then a new skill: the twenty-two faculties (indriya), the "controlling powers" of a life.
Earth cannot give up its own character and take on another's. Master Cháng Bǎi: earth is firm, water moist, fire warm, wind moving.

Master Cháng Bǎi: the foundations of mindfulness are practised when no affliction is active; one must at least subdue the afflictions. Dispute comes from firm attachments and an afflicted mind. Seeing the Buddha "by the ultimate" means giving up contentious views and desires.
Bodhisattvas on the grounds cannot deliberately harm beings or turn back from the mind of awakening.

subs.head: Not the same as dependent origination

blocks.text: Dependent origination is knowledge of how cause and effect arise; this skill is knowledge of the undistorted principle of all things.

"Dominant meaning is the meaning of faculty." Six faculties grasp objects; two (male, female) concern lineage; one is life; five feelings experience karma's fruit; five (faith to wisdom) are for worldly purity; three for transcendent purity. Master Cháng Bǎi: without life, nothing else can be discussed.
Master Cháng Bǎi: through the five feelings craving arises, so these are strongest in generating defilement; with faith and the rest, purity arises.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the ripened body varies according to what the mind does.
Master Cháng Bǎi: any life better than the last is increase; but within the three realms, increase is still a mass of suffering.
The twenty-two faculties are a map of a life: senses, gender, life itself, feelings, the spiritual faculties, and the faculties of awakening.

quiz.q: In the gate of manifestation, what is valid regarding earth and its own mark?
options: earth can become water, as after earthquakes land turns to marsh, the elements changing into each other
earth not relinquishing its mark; earth firm, water moist, fire warm, wind moving, each keeping its mark
the elements have no marks
only wind keeps its mark
quiz.why: The treatise says earth cannot relinquish its own characteristic and take on that of another element. Master Cháng Bǎi: speaking of manifest phenomena, earth is firm, water moist, fire warm, wind moving, each keeping its own mark. The gate continues with faculties and with greed not coexisting with freedom from attachment.

quiz.q: The English has "while not having severed greed and every other ... affliction currently manifest." Is "severed" fitting?
options: fitting: before the mindfulnesses all seeds of affliction must be severed forever, which is why ordinary beings can never cultivate them and why the English is right
纏 is manifest binding; the lecture says it must at least be subdued, practice needing no manifest affliction; "severed" says too much
unfitting: the mindfulnesses are unrelated to affliction
unfitting: the Chinese speaks of severing wholesome roots
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the mindfulnesses are practised when no affliction is manifest; with manifest affliction they cannot be practised; one must at least subdue these afflictions. The Chinese word 纏 limits this to manifest binding. The English "currently manifest" keeps that, but "severed" in English suggests final removal, which comes only much later on the path.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain contentious views, desires, and mind?
options: they are ordinary afflictions of greed and hatred, with no bearing on differences of view about the Dharma, so nothing in thought needs to be examined in this passage
all three are wholesome, disputing to protect the Dharma
dispute comes from firm attachment to ideas, a wish to dispute, and a mind joined with affliction; contentious view arises from clashing views
all three belong only to outsiders
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: dispute comes from firm attachments in thought, together with a wish to dispute and a mind joined with affliction; dispute based on views, differences of ideas, is contentious view. So the treatise says that one holding these cannot truly behold the Tathāgata. What counts is inner relinquishing, not outward presence.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi match 若捨若許 to seeing the Buddha ultimately and conventionally?
options: 捨 is abandoning the Buddha and 許 vowing to see him, both conventional, ultimate seeing being impossible
捨 is giving; 許 is taking precepts
捨 is ordination; 許 is lay life
relinquishing contention and seeing is ultimate; being permitted to see his body with divine or fleshly eye is conventional
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: relinquishing contentious views, desires, and mind and seeing the Buddha is seeing by the ultimate; being permitted to see his physical form by divine or fleshly eye is seeing by the conventional. Those who see only by conventional sight, lacking wisdom, cannot be said to truly see the Buddha.

quiz.q: What can bodhisattvas who have entered the ground levels not do?
options: attain unsurpassed awakening, tenth-ground bodhisattvas never being able to become buddhas
deliberately give rise to harmful intent towards beings, or regress from the awakening-mind
cultivate the four mindfulnesses
save beings
quiz.why: The treatise says bodhisattvas who have entered the ground levels cannot deliberately harm beings or regress from the awakening-mind. Master Cháng Bǎi: bodhisattvas from the first to the tenth ground have accumulated merit that, like the great earth, reaches everywhere. The same passage says an omniscient one cannot fail to know the knowable.

quiz.q: On which four principles rest the further four valid and invalid?
options: the four truths, the root of all principle, on which these four rest
the faculties of faith, diligence, mindfulness, concentration
relativity, function, proof, and intrinsic nature
the four elements
quiz.why: The treatise names relativity, function, proof, and intrinsic nature. Master Cháng Bǎi: the arising of aggregates depends on causes and conditions, and their designation on names; proof uses perception, inference, and scripture to show that what the Buddha taught is true; intrinsic nature is phenomena's being so, unalterable.

quiz.q: How do the skilful understandings of dependent origination and of the valid and invalid differ?
options: the undistorted principle of all is the former; how cause and result arise the latter, the former being wider
they are exactly the same
clear correct wisdom only of how cause and result arise is the former; of the undistorted principle of all is the latter
the former belongs to bodhisattvas, the latter to hearers
quiz.why: The treatise says the first is clear correct wisdom only of how cause and effect arise, the second of the undistorted principle of all things. Master Cháng Bǎi: the first knows the principle of arising; the second discerns whether all dependently arisen phenomena accord with principle. The English "correct wisdom" does not show that this is the noble ones' wisdom.

quiz.q: The English §15 lists eight meanings of faculty. Are these the treatise's text?
options: yes: all eight are treatise text, listed directly, the lecturer adding nothing, so all may be cited as treatise
no: the eight were invented by the translator
no: the eight come from the Treatise on Consciousness-Only
no: the treatise has only 增上義是根義; the rest is the lecturer's citation of the Great Commentary, fascicle 142
quiz.why: The treatise answers only that dominant meaning is the meaning of faculty. Master Cháng Bǎi adds that the Great Commentary, fascicle 142, lists eight meanings; both the Chinese and English sections here have merged that citation into the text. He explains 增上 as one thing exerting strong influence on another, a strong condition for its arising.

quiz.q: How are the twenty-two grouped in the first scheme?
options: five grasping objects; three for family; two for life; four for fruit; six for worldly purity; two for transcendent purity
six grasping objects; two for family; one for life; five experiencing karma's fruit; five for worldly purity; three for transcendent purity
all twenty-two grasp objects, that being the definition of faculty, other groupings being for convenience
only the five of faith and the rest are true faculties
quiz.why: The treatise sets six for grasping objects, two for family lineage, one for life, five for experiencing karma's fruit, five for worldly purity, and three for transcendent purity. Master Cháng Bǎi: the strongest force for an unbroken family is the male and female faculties. Five further schemes follow, each dividing the twenty-two.

quiz.q: Which are the five experiencing karma's fruit, and do faith and the rest belong only to worldly purity?
options: the five physical faculties; faith and the rest are only worldly, the transcendent having only the three, with no overlap
faith and the rest; none belong to purity
mind and four feelings; faith and the rest are only transcendent
the five feelings; faith and the rest extend not only to worldly but also to transcendent purity
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: pleasant and unpleasant conditions in life are karma's fruit, and it is the five feeling faculties that experience them. He adds that faith and the rest extend not only to worldly purity but also to transcendent purity, though the scheme lists them under the former.

quiz.q: The English has "the means by which life's activities continue" for 為活性命事業方便. How does its aim differ from the lecture's?
options: the lecture: life is the means to successful enterprise; enterprise is the aim, so the English is exact
the lecture: activities are the means by which life survives; life is the aim, and the English reverses this to activities continuing
the lecture: the life faculty is a means of practice
the lecture: the life faculty has nothing to do with activities
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: taking various activities as means so that life can survive and continue, the life faculty is established; without life nothing else can be discussed. So the structure is activities serving life. The English "the means by which life's activities continue" turns life into something that serves activities.

quiz.q: How is the name of the aspirant's faculty 未知欲知根 explained?
options: 未知 is worldly ignorance; 欲知 is the wish to learn during study, and so all ordinary beings have it
未知 is not knowing karma; 欲知 is wishing to know the next life
未知 is not yet knowing the noble path or realising the Dharma; 欲知 is the wholesome wish to realise truth
未知 is an arhat's unknowing; 欲知 is the Buddha's omniscience
quiz.why: The treatise sets three faculties for transcendent purity. Master Cháng Bǎi on the first: 未知 means not yet knowing the noble path or the Dharma, not yet having realised it; 欲知 is the wholesome aspiration to realise the truth of the Dharma. The English "the aspirant's faculty" brings out the second half only.

quiz.q: In the second scheme, what are the two for hidden objects and the one for the temporal boundary?
options: eye and ear; the mind faculty, since these cannot see the hidden and mind knows time
the male and female faculties; the life faculty
pain and sorrow; equanimity
faith and wisdom; mindfulness
quiz.why: The treatise sets two faculties for hidden objects and one for the temporal boundary. Master Cháng Bǎi: the male and female faculties are strongest in experiencing what is not visible; the life faculty is strongest regarding the length and limit of time within which objects are experienced.

quiz.q: Why do five feelings stand for affliction arising, and why are the last eight for establishing purity?
options: the five feelings are pure; the last eight are defiled, practice being attachment, so they should be swapped
the five are bodily sensations, unrelated to affliction
the last eight are innate, needing no cultivation
through feeling craving arises, the five being strongest for defilement; faith and the rest as base realise the aspirant's faculty and seeing
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: through feelings of pain, pleasure, sorrow, joy, and equanimity, craving and other afflictions arise, so these five are strongest in generating defilement; with faith and the rest as a foundation one can enter the aspirant's faculty, and on that see the path. So the scheme reads as a path from experience to purification.

quiz.q: The English has "enabling that support to move freely at its own command." What is the problem with the subject?
options: this one is the life faculty: the body moves freely by its lifespan, so the English is exact, unrelated to mind
this one is the body faculty, the body being its own master, so the English is clearer than the Chinese
this one is the male faculty: the body moves with desire
this one is the mind faculty: the body turns according to what mind creates; the English makes the body its own master
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the ripened body on which beings depend varies according to what the consciousness born of the mind faculty does. So this faculty is the mind, which makes the support turn at will. The English "at its own command" reads as if the body commanded itself, which obscures the role of mind.

quiz.q: The English has "surpassing rebirth" and "decisive superiority" for 勝生 and 定勝. How does the lecture divide these?
options: 勝生 is only rebirth from human to god, and 定勝 is attaining absorption, both of which lie within the three realms, so the English word "decisive" is much too strong
each life better than the last is increase; nirvāṇa with no further birth is decisive; the English serves but does not show these as paths
both mean buddhahood
both mean birth in a wealthy family
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: it need not mean human to god; any life better than the last is increase; but with results in the three realms, though it is increase, it is still a mass of suffering; entering nirvāṇa, with no more results in the three realms, is decisive victory. The familiar terms are the paths of increase and of decisive excellence.
